newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland football stadium reaches seat sales goal.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland football stadium reaches seat sales goal.

text.p: A Cleveland Browns football team will play in its namesake city again now that a sales goal has been reached to sell luxury seats at a new stadium, city and National Football League officials announced Tuesday.

Seat sales totaled $13.5 million so far, exceeding the $9.42 million sales requirment by Jan 31 under an agreement between Cleveland and the NFL, according to a news release from Mayor Michael White's office.

By meeting the sales goal, Cleveland will get a football team to replace the former Browns organization, which moved to Baltimore in 1995 and renamed itself the Ravens, and a NFL contribution of up to $48 million for stadium construction costs, the release said.
The new team and new stadium are expected for the 1999 football season, the release added.
Meanwhile, Cleveland is moving forward with plans to finance its share of the stadium, currently estimated to cost $242 million.
Martin Carmody, Cleveland's finance director, said last week the city plans to sell $130 million to $140 million of certificates of participation in March.
The COPs would be paid off with revenues from taxes on parking, admissions and car rentals. A.G. Edwards & Sons has been selected to lead the deal, he added.
In addition to the NFL contribution, Cleveland is also counting on a state of Ohio grant for the stadium.
